text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Stocks ended lower as the antics of the volatile Dow scared investors away and another call for higher interest rates by the Bank of England pushed bonds lower. The FTSE 100 share index ended 29.9 points lower at 4,207.5.

FRANKFURT - Overnight volatility on Wall Street and a see-saw response to key U.S. economic data in the afternoon unsettled the stock market, and prices finally ended the day at lower levels. The IBIS DAX index, which tracks all-day screen dealings in German blue chips, closed the day at 2,997.95. Earlier, the DAX index, which was catching up on a surge in late screen trading Tuesday, ended floor trade at 2,999.20, 9.87 points higher than Tuesday's midafternoon close.

PARIS - Stocks finished a nervous session in a loss but off intraday lows as a rising Dow rode to the rescue in the afternoon. Traders said Paris dipped to a loss of 1.5 percent as the markets whipsawed after a U.S. durable goods report showed a 1.7 percent fall instead of an expected increase. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 17.75 points at 2,465.01.

ZURICH - A stronger opening on Wall Street led to a recovery of Swiss stocks in late trade, but Swiss indexes still ended weaker after Tuesday's record close. Dealers said worries about a possible U.S. interest rate hike may keep a lid on the market ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting Feb. 4-5. The all-share SPI fell 10.04 points to 2,666.63 points.

TOKYO - Stocks rose sharply, as the yen's fall to a fresh 47-month low against the dollar fuelled buying of stocks in multinational companies. The market's key barometer, the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares, jumped by 538.73 points or 3.03 percent, to close at 18,335.30.

HONG KONG - Stocks ended with heavy losses, beaten down by interest rate concerns and a slide in the property sector after recommendations that banks curb lending for luxury property acquisitions. The Hang Seng Index fell 117.86 points to 13,285.43. Turnover was HK$11.89 billion vs. Tuesday's HK$8.64 billion.

SYDNEY - The stock market kept a firm grip on its gains to close higher with options-related trade ahead of Thursday's January expiry and well-received inflation data underpinning the rise. The All Ordinaries index added 10.0 points to 2,414.2.

JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares took a battering as the bullion price lost all of Tuesday's gains and fell to $351 an ounce, threatening to test the key $350-an-ounce level. Gold stocks, having climbed nearly 5 percent Tuesday, riding the brief rally in the gold price, shed more than 3 percent. The gold index lost 43.8 points to 1,385.3 points. Industrial stocks also took a beating, with the index shedding 58 points to 8,011.0. Weakness in gold and industrial stocks combined to knock the all-share index 48.5 points down to 6,687.5.
